{{Quote|You can't stop change any more than you can stop the suns from setting.|Shmi Skywalker, to her son Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />}}
'''Shmi Skywalker Lars''' was the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Parent/Legends|mother]] of the [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. She was sold into [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] at an early age. In [[41 BBY/Legends|41 BBY]], Shmi gave birth to a son she named Anakin, who was born without a father but strongly connected with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Although her son was enslaved as well, Shmi remained with him and cared for him greatly, willing to do anything to help him. Six [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after Anakin left to become a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], she was sold to [[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]], who freed her. The pair subsequently married and lived in the [[Lars homestead/Legends|Lars homestead]] alongside Cliegg's son, [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen]], and Owen's partner, [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|Beru Whitesun]]. Just before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Shmi died in her son's arms after being brutally [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] by a band of [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
Shmi Skywalker was born in [[72 BBY/Legends|72 BBY]]<ref name="Birth Date" /> from unnamed parents. At the [[66 BBY/Legends|age of six]], Shmi and her parents embarked on a space voyage to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], where they were captured by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and sold into slavery.<ref name="TPM VD">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

===Struggles in slavery===
{{Quote|The Republic doesn't exist out here. We must survive on our own.|Shmi, to Padmé Amidala|<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />}}
While some of these masters were cruel, others were kind&mdash;notably [[Pi-Lippa]], who taught Shmi valuable technical skills. Though Pi-Lippa had planned to free Shmi, she'd died before she could, and Shmi instead became the property of one of Pi-Lippa's relatives, who did not want to free her.<ref name="DB" />

[[File:AnakinShmi.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Shmi and Anakin arrive on Tatooine to serve Gardulla the Hutt.]]
Around this time Shmi discovered that she was pregnant and gave birth to a son she named Anakin. Shmi would say that her son was conceived without a father, but she could not explain how it happened. Nevertheless, she gladly accepted his birth and raised him.<ref name="birthplanet">In ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' it is implied that Anakin was indeed born on Tatooine. However, the [http://www.blueharvest.net/scoops/pm-script.shtml shooting script] for [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] includes dialogue where Anakin clarifies that he and Shmi arrived on the planet at the age of three. (which would equate to around the year [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]])</ref> Three years later, Shmi and her son came into the ownership of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla the Elder]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /> Gardulla was a cruel master and had little regard for the safety of Shmi and her son, as evident when she allowed young Skywalker to participate in the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]], believing Anakin to be incapable of winning.<ref name="Podracing Tales">"[[Podracing Tales]]"</ref>

[[File:ShmiAnniemoment.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Shmi and Anakin at Watto's shop.]]
A few months after her arrival to Mos Espa, Gardulla lost ownership of the two in a bet, and Shmi and Anakin became the property of the junk dealer [[Watto/Legends|Watto]].<ref name="Podracing Tales" /> However, like Gardulla, Watto was often found to be quite harsh, seldom showing his softer side to the two. Under Watto's care, they were afforded simple luxuries and were allowed to have very few personal possessions.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /> When not performing tasks given to her by Watto, Shmi spent most of her time worrying about her adventurous son. Whether it was to recover parts for Watto or going out of his way to help someone in need, Anakin often managed to get himself into trouble. Shmi did little to discourage his tendency, though she began to fear that she was going to lose him someday.<ref name="Episode I: Anakin Skywalker">''[[Episode I: Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref> The two were very close, and despite not having enough money, Anakin showered Shmi with simple gifts to show his affection. At other times, he built inventions to sell or use to lighten her workload.<ref name="DB2">{{DB|character|anakinskywalker|Skywalker, Anakin}}</ref> One such invention was a [[C-3PO/Legends|protocol droid]] Anakin had found and managed to scrape together using old parts he gathered from Watto's junkyard.<ref name="Thank the Maker">{{Tales|6|Thank the Maker}}</ref>

Shmi became aware of Anakin's gifts and hid as much as she could from Watto, though she could not hide Anakin's natural piloting abilities. After discovering this almost by accident, Watto let the boy continue his piloting, believing he could gain potential profit from the venture. Anakin proved to be an excellent pilot despite the fact that he had never been able to finish a race. To her relief, Anakin managed to come out unharmed, save for a few bruises, though she hated watching him drive in what she referred to as "those awful races". Though she never said so, Anakin thought that his mother believed that simply by being there she could keep him from coming to harm.<ref name="TPMN" /> She secretly wished for Anakin to have a better life as his gifts made her realize that he wasn't meant to be enslaved.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />

===A mother's sacrifice===
{{Quote|Son, my place is here. My future is here. It is time for you to let go&hellip;to let go of me. I cannot go with you.|Shmi, to Anakin|<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />}}
[[File:Anakinandmom.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Shmi and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin]] part ways.]]
One day after returning to the [[Slave Quarters Row/Legends|hovel]] that she and her son shared, Shmi met the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], and his companions from [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]: [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] and their [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]. Shmi offered the group her hospitality and place to stay during a raging sandstorm that enveloped Mos Espa. Like Anakin, Shmi initially believed that these strangers arrived on Tatooine to free enslaved people. This proved not to be the case when they recounted to Anakin their plight of how they ended up being stranded on Tatooine on a diplomatic mission to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Anakin offered to help his newfound friends repair their ship, forming a plan that included Qui-Gon sponsoring him in the upcoming Boonta Eve Classic. Shmi, however, disagreed. It was only when Anakin recalled her words on helping others that Shmi allowed Anakin to help the strangers, claiming that he was meant to help them.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />

As she watched Anakin build [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|his podracer]], Shmi revealed to Qui-Gon Anakin's miraculous birth. When Qui-Gon remarked that his presence in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] was unusually strong, Shmi hopefully asked if he was able to help Anakin. Instead of getting the answer she had hoped for, the Jedi Master replied that he's unsure, given that he truly wasn't on Tatooine to free enslaved beings.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />

[[File:Shmi.png|thumb|right|200px|Shmi watches her son leave to become a Jedi.]]
The next day, Shmi accompanied the group to the Boonta Eve Classic, where she tensely watched the race from afar. Unbeknownst to her, before the start of the race, Qui-Gon made a bet with Watto for the freedom of Shmi and Anakin. Watto, however, wouldn't have it, claiming that no podracer was worth two enslaved beings. Because of his interest in the boy, Qui-Gon opted to free Anakin, using his powers to tamper with the [[Chance cube/Legends|chance cube]] Watto had brought out to decide which of the two would be freed. To her surprise and theirs, Anakin won the race, and likewise, his freedom. Shmi joined Anakin in the crowd of admirers, and the two shared a brief mother-and-son moment with Shmi telling Anakin how proud she was of him.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />

After securing Anakin's earnings from the race, Qui-Gon informed Shmi of Anakin's freedom and of his intention to train the boy as a Jedi. He was, however, unable to secure her freedom. It was then that Shmi had to make the most difficult decision in her life: letting go of her son. Comforted by Qui-Gon, she watched as Anakin prepared himself to leave, the latter stopping a few times to express his doubts about leaving home. She advised him to let go, claiming that her place and future was on Tatooine. This prompted Anakin to leave with the Jedi Master, but not before promising that he would return and free her.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />

===Freedom===
{{Quote|It is you I feel closest to ... The Magister's peoples made me their servant, and you were a slave. I did what they told me to do. You did what your owner told you to do. So like me! I tried to be like others, but I am not like them. My mind is made up of so many parts, spread out over so much of my world. And your mind is so different from the others. I have no real parents, and your parents&mdash;|[[Zonama Sekot/Legends|Sekot]], the intelligent essence of the planet Zonama Sekot, likens 12-year-old Anakin Skywalker's prodigious mind, his enslavement, and his unique parentage to its own|<ref name="Rogue Planet">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref>}}
While her son trained with the Jedi, Shmi remained in the service of Watto. Watto had since then toned down his gruff demeanor, treating Shmi with more respect than he previously had, and on occasion, foraging for the both of them during hard times.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]''</ref>

Shmi came across the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Vilmarh Grahrk|Villie]] while Watto wiled him into buying faulty [[DUM-series pit droid/Legends|pit droids]] to compensate for the debt owed to him by the Toydarian. Villie fell for Watto's ruse and took possession of the droids. As ordered by her master, Shmi gathered the droids and brought them to Villie's ship, ''Inferno'', choosing not to inform the Devaronian of Watto's deceit.<ref name="Bad Business">{{Tales|8|Bad Business}}</ref>

Eventually, Watto's business began to decline due to his excessive betting on podraces, further discrediting his reputation as a successful junk dealer.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> Around [[26 BBY/Legends|26 BBY]],<ref name="UVG">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''</ref> his losses were so bad that he was forced to sell Shmi to [[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]], a moisture farmer who had fallen in love with her.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> Watto made several excuses and created a number of delays in the transaction, torn between the loss of his only enslaved person and his hope that she would be happy with Lars. With her help, Cliegg and his son Owen tricked Watto into selling Shmi in exchange for a [[Tobal lens]]<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /> provided to them by a friend of the late Qui-Gon Jinn in the Jedi Order.<ref name="FF113">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 113|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 113]]</ref> Watto later admitted to deactivating her slave transmitter shortly after Anakin's departure for a fear that Shmi would wander aimlessly off in her sorrow and blow herself up. When Cliegg asked for her hand in marriage, Shmi agreed. She found that she had fallen in love with Cliegg, as well as finding familiar affection towards Owen, and wanted to be a part of their lives.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" />

In attendance at their wedding were Owen, Cliegg and Owen's friends, and Anakin's friends [[Kitster Chanchani Banai]], [[W. Wald]], and [[Amee/Legends|Amee]]. Watto surprised them all by showing up uninvited. He then offered Cliegg a discount on used parts and told Shmi times grew hard on the moisture farm and Wald wasn't doing such a good job as his assistant.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" />

They lived a quiet existence on the Lars Homestead as moisture farmers, forming a strong bond of a loving family.<ref name="EpIInovel">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>

Shmi often told her new family how much she missed her son Anakin, telling them stories of his misadventures. Despite finding a place among the Lars family, Shmi still longed to see her son. Every night, she held a vigil for Anakin, hoping that he would return from the stars.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" />

During her years with the Lars family, she kept a journal where she recorded events almost everyday in hopes if Anakin returned from his Jedi training. This journal would eventually come into the possession of her granddaughter [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] many years later. From reading the [[Holojournal/Legends|holojournal]], Leia gained a faint sense of what her father was like before becoming Darth Vader and learned to forgive him.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" />

===Reunited with Anakin and death===
{{Quote|I'm so proud of you, Ani<!-- This is how it's spelled in the DVD subtitles. Don't change it. -->&hellip; so proud&hellip; I missed you so much&hellip; now I am complete&hellip;|Shmi Skywalker|<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />}}
[[File:ShmiCapture-AOTCComic.jpg|thumb|left|Shmi is kidnapped by Tusken Raiders.]]
Just a month before the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] began attacking outlying moisture farms. One morning, Shmi went out to pick [[Vaporator mushroom/Legends|vaporator mushrooms]] from the [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|moisture vaporators]], but was kidnapped by a group of Tuskens on her way home. Cliegg assembled a search team in an attempt to locate her, but ended up losing 26 out of the 30 that were sent out and his right leg. After a month, he decided to give up the search, believing Shmi to be dead. In actuality, Shmi was still, just barely, alive&mdash;severely beaten and dehydrated, holding on to her memories of Anakin in an effort to stay alive. Shmi's resilience fascinated the Tusken Raiders, prompting them to try other methods of torturing; however, it only strengthened her resolve to live long enough to see her son. During her captivity, Shmi often reached out to Anakin, hoping that he would come and rescue her.<ref name="EpIInovel" />

[[File:Shmidyng.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Shmi dies in the arms of her son.]]

Through their strong bond with one another, Anakin was overcome with nightmares of his mother, in which he had sensed her pain and suffering. Unable to bear them any longer, Anakin traveled to Tatooine to find her, bringing [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] with him. Upon their arrival in Mos Espa, they were told by Watto that he had sold Shmi to Cliegg Lars, who had freed and married her. At the [[Lars homestead/Legends|Lars homestead]], he encountered his old droid, [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], and the Lars family. A heartbroken Cliegg recounted to Anakin's mother, Shmi's abduction and the settlers' attempt to save her. He tried to convince Skywalker that it was impossible for Shmi to have survived, but Anakin wouldn't have it. In his disbelief, Anakin set out to find her, leaving Padmé in the care of the Lars. Using his senses, Anakin managed to locate her inside a Tusken Raider encampment, bound to a rack at the side of a tent, and bearing scars from weeks of beatings. After Anakin untied her from her bindings, the two engaged in a short conversation with Anakin comforting her in a vain effort to keep her alive. With her final breaths, Shmi managed to whisper her love for him before quietly dying in his arms.<ref name="EpIInovel" /><ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />

Anakin allowed the shock of her death to catalyze an explosion of his long-nursed anger and selfishness, and thus, the beginning of his path to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. He flew into a rage, killing every Tusken Raider in the encampment—even, as he confessed to Padmé later, "not just the men.. but the women.. and the children too." After the [[Mission to rescue Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|massacre]], he returned to the tent to wrap her body, and took her back to the Lars homestead, where a [[Funeral of Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|small funeral]] was held. In front of her grave, Anakin voiced his regret that he could not save her, and promised not to let anything of the sort happen again.<ref name="EpIInovel" /><ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|I wasn't strong enough to save you, Mom. I wasn't strong enough. But I promise I won't fail again. I miss you...so much.|Anakin Skywalker, as he kneels before the tomb of his mother|<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />}}
As a direct result of Skywalker's earlier massacre against the Tuskens, the other Tusken clans referred to her in passing as a witch and the mate of the [[Great Jawenko]].<ref name="Barely Tolerable 2">{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-2|series=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[File:ShmiAnakinCloneWars.png|thumb|left|200px|[[Son/Legends|Son]] appears as Shmi to Anakin in a vision on [[Mortis/Legends|Mortis]]]]

In the decades following Shmi's death, she was remembered for starting the [[Skywalker family/Legends|Skywalker family]]. Her old friend [[Sorna]] came to the Lars homestead every year to place flowers on her grave.<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Flowers for Shmi|Tatooine}}</ref> Anakin saw his mother again in a [[Force vision/Legends|Force vision]] around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]] on [[Mortis/Legends|Mortis]]. The vision was induced by the [[Son/Legends|Son]], one of the powerful Force-wielders controlling the [[Planet/Legends|planet]], through which the current of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] flowed. Anakin's vision of Shmi told him that he was not at fault for letting her die but that he had drawn the burden of guilt around himself. When Anakin revealed to Shmi that he was married to Amidala, whom Shmi had met in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Shmi told him that Anakin's wife did not represent his true destiny. His vision of Shmi then disappeared, but not before briefly taking the form of the Son.<ref name="Overlords">{{TCW|Overlords}}</ref>

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Anakin's wife Padmé gave birth to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and died soon afterward, having lost the will to live, as a result of Anakin Skywalker, the man she loved, turning to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. The twins were separated by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]: Leia was adopted by the childless couple [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]] and his [[Breha Organa/Legends|wife]]; Luke was adopted by Owen and Beru Lars.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>

[[File:Tatooine_ghost_illustration_scene.jpg|thumb|220x220px|Shmi's granddaughter Leia found her holojournal.]]
In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], Leia discovered Shmi's [[Holojournal/Legends|holojournal]] at the old Lars Homestead, now in the possession of the [[Darklighter family/Legends|Darklighter family]]. By watching the [[Holojournal/Legends|holojournal]], Leia learned about the Skywalker family before the Clone Wars and discovered how Shmi had died. Leia also learned compassion and forgiveness for her father and as a result she planned to start a family with Solo.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" />

A year after<ref name="The Essential Reader's Companion">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> her journal was discovered,<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /> Leia gave birth to Han Solo's children, [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] and [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]].<ref name="The Last Command">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> During the Emperor's return, Leia gave birth to her's and Han's third child, [[Anakin Solo]],<ref name="Dark Empire II 6">[[Dark Empire II 6|''Dark Empire II'' 6]]</ref> who would die during the [[Mission to Myrkr]].<ref name=":0">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref> In [[26 ABY/Legends|26.5 ABY]],<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force real-life book">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] gave birth to her and Luke Skywalker's child, [[Ben Skywalker]].<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory II: Rebirth">''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory II: Rebirth]]''</ref> Ten years later, [[Tenel Ka Djo|Tenel Ka]] gave birth to Jacen Solo's child, [[Allana Djo Solo|Allana]], making Allana<ref name="Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref> Shmi's great-great-grandchild.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /> Although Jacen and Anakin died,<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref><ref name=":0" /> their sister Jaina Solo married into the [[Fel dynasty]].<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>

By the time of the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], over a hundred years after the death of Shmi Skywalker, her legacy and the name of her family lived on through her last known descendants: [[Kol Skywalker]],<ref name=":1">[[Legacy (2006) 1|''Legacy'' (2006) 1]]</ref> [[Rawk|Nat Skywalker]] and his nephew,<ref name="Legacy 2006 24">[[Legacy (2006) 24|''Legacy'' (2006) 24]]</ref> [[Cade Skywalker]].<ref name=":1" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I... I love&mdash;|Shmi's last words|<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />}}
[[File:ShmiTucksAnakin.png|thumb|right|200px|Shmi Skywalker resting her son in bed]]
Shmi was kind, peaceful, compassionate and polite, despite her years of slavery. She was selfless, willing to sacrifice anything for her son. She loved and cared for Anakin more than anything, and desperately wanted him to have a better life, knowing that there was something special about him. It was because of her love and sense that he had a special destiny that she allowed him to go to Coruscant to become a Jedi, knowing she would likely never see him again. She was befuddled by his birth however, as it seemed Anakin had "no father".<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /> She cared for Cliegg Lars, her husband, following Anakin's departure and his son, Owen Lars, despite the fact that he was not her true son. Years later, her husband additionally described her as loving, "the best partner a man could ask for".<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />

Even though Watto had mistreated Shmi and her son for years, she still was able to see the good in him, and after Anakin left, comforted him. Watto in turn became a kinder master, giving Shmi small gifts. Shmi still treated him well, again showing her kind nature and willingness to forgive.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" />

She earned a small income cleaning computer memory devices. Like her son, Shmi could fix almost anything. One of Shmi's former masters was [[Pi-Lippa]], who taught Shmi various technical skills. These abilities increased Shmi's perceived value for slavers, but unfortunate circumstances led her to becoming enslaved by Watto. She was always on the lookout for discarded tools in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]], and her dwelling was filled with mechanical and electronic devices like Anakin's. She did the best she could to raise her son, encouraging Anakin's interest in technology, and hoped their skills would one day liberate them from slavery.

==Behind the scenes==
The character was portrayed by Swedish actress [[Pernilla August]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /><ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> That Anakin Skywalker's mother would be named Shmi and that August would portray her were announced in [[1998]]. The [[original trilogy]] was [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|rereleased in theaters and VHS]] to commemorate the twenty year anniversary of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] [[1997|the year before]] and ''[[Star Wars Trivial Pursuit]]'' was released to coincide with this. The limited edition game contained a sequestered pack of questions that served as a preview of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|the first new trilogy installment]], two of which divulged those bits of information. One of the first drafts for her name was [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Warka]].

In [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''The Phantom Menace'' game adaptation]], Shmi Skywalker is voiced by [[Carolyn Seymour]]. In the game, Qui-Gon Jinn, controlled by the player, can kill Shmi during the level ''Encounter in the Desert'' with no reason. However, as this strongly contradicts the existing storyline, it is non-[[canon]].<ref name="TPMvg">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>

Pernilla August reprised the role of Shmi Skywalker in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|season 3]] episode "[[Overlords]]."<ref name="Overlords" />
